MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 10, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell at
5:01 p.m., on October 10, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on October 5, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez ~ arrived 5:02pm
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Labor Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6(a):
  Agency Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Keith
  Rattay; City Attorney William Curley; Labor Attorney Peter Brown: Employee
  Organization: Service Employees’ International Union (SEIU)

 CS2.  Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Dennis Wilberg.

City Council Minutes  1  October 10, 2023
  RECESS AND RECONVENE TO CLOSED SESSION

 At the hour of 5:02 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at
 6:01 pm with all City Council Members present.

 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

 City Attorney Curley announced that there were two closed session items, both pertaining to labor
 negotiations. CS1 pertained to the Union and no reportable action occurred. CS2 pertained to the
 unrepresented and non-union employees, and Council gave direction to increase the employee’s
 medical coverage.

 INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Goodell

 PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Friends of the Library Donation

  Mayor Goodell received donation from Friends of the Library President Kathleen
  Cunningham.

 P2.  Proclaim the Week of October 15 - 21, 2023 To Be National Friends of Libraries Week

  Mayor Goodell presented certificate to Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis
  Hansen.

 P3.  Annual Walk Against Drugs

  Mayor Goodell received presentation from Chief of Police Chris McDonald.

 Mayor Goodell announced two Boy Scouts in the audience, Brayden Guest and Vincent Mays
 working on their Citizenship Merit Badges.

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

 Tom Moore, M.V.: Referenced two reports; the ULI (Urban Land Institute) report from 2007 and
 the Core Area Vision Plan from 2016. He stated that the unsolved commercial area is consistent in
 both of these reports. And, although he supports the Core Area Vision Plan, he suggested the City
 stop perusing these plans and focus on solving the commercial areas.

 William Palma, M.V.: Spoke on the injustices that were directed at him at Crucero Park by the
 Orange County Sheriff’s Department. He addressed his comments to the Attorney General, FBI and
 DOJ with regards to the OSCD. Addressed the role of Church and State.

City Council Minutes  2  October 10, 2023
  Amanda Fritz, M.V.: Spoke in reference to a distasteful Halloween adult display in the front yard of
 one of her neighbors. She provided the Council with photos of the display in question which is
 located at the end of the cul-de-sac, near Castile Elementary School. She stated neighbors and parents
 are concerned about the young children in the neighborhood, and have asked the display be removed
 or changed, however, the display has only grown in size. Complaints have been made to City and
 she is looking for support and a response to help remove the distasteful display.

 Arron Hand, M.V.: Spoke of concerns regarding the City’s electoral dysfunction, and the legal costs
 associated with it. He commented on the Nadadores contract and praised Council Member Vasquez
 on her questions and shame on the Council for silencing her voice. He questioned the staff report,
 and Mayor Goodell abstaining from the vote as a Board Member of the Nadadores. He concluded
 by stating the public deserves accountability and transparency.

 City Attorney Curley clarified Mr. Hand’s comments and properly defended the three individual
 Council Members in question.

 Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated Rabbi Marcus asked her to invite residents to the community gathering
 in support of Israel at the Village Green on Wednesday, October 11 at 6pm. She spoke of the
 September 26 minutes she challenged, and Mayor Goodell’s financial conflict of interest pertaining
 to the Nadadores contract. She added that government should follow the rules, and not pick and
 choose. She also thanked Council Member Vasquez for being prepared and asking questions of the
 Nadadores contract, and shamed the remainder of the Council for calling the question when she still
 had concerns to address.

 City Attorney Curley stated the Council has done nothing wrong.

 City Manager Wilberg commented on Mr. Hand and Ms. Schlicht’s comments of subsidy to the
 Nadadores. He stated, if the City was to operate the complex it would cost over $3 million dollars a
 year, however, the current cost to the City is a little over $300,000, thus saving the City over $2.5
 million dollars. Thus, he has a real problem with people continuing to characterize it as the City
 subsiding over $2.5 million dollars.

 Michele Mitchell, M.V.: Thanked the Council and staff for their great work and leadership, thus
 making Mission Viejo a great place to live. She commented on the naysayers and listed all facilities
 that are an investment of tax dollars, from the improved golf course, to the recreation centers, the
 library, the animal shelter, the condition of the streets and landscape, programs, entertainment, and
 amenities offered at all facilities, and the Orange County Sheriff’s Department for making Mission
 Viejo safe. She concluded by thanking everyone again for making her hometown safe, beautiful,
 entertaining and something to be proud of.

 Robert Breton, M.V.: Spoke of vicious savagery and the slaughter of innocent women and children
 in Israel. He voiced concerns for the Jewish members in Mission Viejo, and asked the Council to
 consider three things. 1) Increased OCSD security for Rabbi Marcus and the Chabad Center, 2)
 promote and attend the candlelit vigil at the Village Green on October 11, and, 3) publicize and attend
 the forum hosted by the Greater Interfaith Council of Saddleback Valley this Sunday at 4pm at Saint
 Georges Episcopal Church in Lake Forest.

City Council Minutes  3  October 10, 2023
  Barbara Casserly, M.V.: Spoke of the unacceptable council behavior toward Council Member
 Vasquez at the last council meeting, and chastise them for not allowing Council Member Vasquez
 continue her questioning of the Nadadores contract. She also told the Council to stop fighting a losing
 court battle of the illegal extension of Council terms and to use the funds towards affordable swim
 lessons. She questioned why the only Gen X member is not on the CUSD committee. Questioned
 Council Member Bucknum representing the City on committees related to real estate. She concluded
 by listing all the thing she loves about Mission Viejo and reminded the Council to be Respectful, the
 Character word for October.

 Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: Thanked the Council for recognizing the Library. She addressed the severe
 lack of civility towards Council Member Vasquez at the last Council meeting with regards to her
 thorough, yet slightly long questioning of the Nadadores contract. She criticized Council Member
 Bucknum and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley for calling the question when Council Member Vasquez still
 had further questions.

 Saga Conroy, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of Orange County Supervisor Don Wagner and announced
 two upcoming events. County of Orange Older Adults Needs Assessment on October 12 from Noon
 - 2pm at the Norman P. Murray Community Center, and The BIG Jump event where Mayor Goodell
 and Supervisor Wagner shall jump of a 30ft platform on Sunday, October 29, from 2-4pm at the
 Nadadores Complex.

 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley addressed the criticism over the way the Nadadores contract discussion
 occurred at the last Council meeting. She clarified that the Council follow the Rules of Order and
 were in compliance. The agenda item lasted an hour and 15 minutes with other items on the agenda,
 thus the need to keep the meeting on pace. Lastly, she stated all Council Members have access to
 the City Manager and staff ahead of time to ask questions, and it was clear that four members were
 in support of the contract and she felt it appropriate to call the question.

 Council Member Ruesch asked Captain McDonald to look into the Halloween display matter.

 Council Member Bucknum asked if Code Enforcement could also look into the Halloween display
 matter. She also asked Captain McDonald for an overview to Mr. Breton’s comments.

 Captain McDonald provided a response to both comments made by Mr. Breton and Ms. Fritz.

 Mayor Goodell added that he and City Manager Wilberg had a positive meeting with the
 Representative from the Governor’s Office earlier today and talked of some of the challenges facing
 Mission Viejo.

 CONSENT CALENDAR

 Item 13 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

 Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to approve the
 Consent Calendar as outlined below.

City Council Minutes  4  October 10, 2023
  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
 NOES:  None
 ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of September 26, 2023, as
  presented.

 2.  General Check Register Dated September 15, 2023 in the Amount of $1,280,439.94

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 3.  General Check Register Dated September 22, 2023 in the Amount of $1,836,232.15

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  Golf Check Register Dated September 15, 2023 in the Amount of $283,575.97

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 5.  Golf Check Register Dated September 22, 2023 in the Amount of $14,000.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2023

  Received and filed.

 7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for August 2023

  Received and filed.

 8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for August 2023

  Received and filed.

 9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2023

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  5  October 10, 2023
  10.  Year End Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Fiscal Year Ended June 30,
  2023

  Received and filed.

 11.  Year End Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo Golf Course Fund for Fiscal
  Year Ended June 30, 2023

  Received and filed.

 12.  Purchase of (1) 2024 2500HD Chevrolet Silverado Vehicle – Replacement Animal
  Services Vehicle

  (1) Awarded a Purchase Agreement for one (1) 2024 2500HD Chevrolet Silverado vehicle to
  Guaranty Chevrolet Motors, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $66,100.00, and (2) issued a
  Purchase Order for one (1) 2024 2500HD Chevrolet Silverado vehicle to Guaranty Chevrolet
  Motors, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $66,100.00.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 13.  Orange County Transportation Authority 2023-2024 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects

  Associate Traffic Engineer Mario Gutierrez presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 23-37 Approving the Submittal of the Alicia Parkway Corridor Improvement
  Project to the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) for Funding Under the
  Competitive Measure M2 Regional Transportation Signal Synchronization Program (Project
  P); and (2) direct staff to transmit Resolution 23-37 to OCTA by October 26, 2023, in
  conjunction with the City's funding application for said project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 PUBLIC HEARINGS

 14. Speed Hump Installation on Montanoso Drive

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley recused herself from this agenda item because her residence is
  impacted by the decision.

City Council Minutes  6  October 10, 2023
   Associate Traffic Engineer Mario Gutierrez and Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon
  presented the staff report.

  Council Members asked various questions of staff.

  Mayor Goodell opened the Public Hearing at 7:36 pm.

  Allen Bourgeois, M.V.: Asked staff for a sight distance evaluation for motorists making a
  northbound left-turn along Montanoso onto westbound Via Marina.

  Kevin Donahue, Jonis Smith, Pam Smith, Laszlo Maira-Hazy, Virgil Deering, and Mike
  Peleaux all spoke in support of speed humps.

  Mayor Goodell closed the Public Hearing at 7:55 pm

  Council Members made various comments, asked various questions and directed staff to look
  at the ordinance to see if it can be modernized to meet current standards as necessary.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Vasquez, to
  approve the request for speeds humps to be installed on Montanoso Drive between Oso
  Parkway and Estanciero Drive, contingent upon prior approval by the Planning and
  Transportation Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

The City Council recessed at 8:05 pm and reconvened at 8:08 pm with all five Council Members
present.

 NEW BUSINESS

 15.  Fiscal Year 2022/23 Close Out Report and Fiscal Year 2023/24 Budget Adjustments for
  Certain Revenue and Expenditure Accounts

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Members asked various questions of staff.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 23-38 Amending the FY 2022/23 Budget for Year-End Close Out Adjustments in
  Certain Accounts and Funds; (2) adopted Resolution 23-39 Amending the FY 2023/24
  Budget; and (3) adopt Resolution 23-40 Amending the Authorized Position Schedule.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  7  October 10, 2023
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 16.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Goodell.

 17.  Economic Development Committee Report

  Received report from City Manager Wilberg. Council Member Ruesch added that tomorrow’s
  Los Osos Project Update is the seventh input session for the public. Mayor Goodell stated he
  is leaving on Sunday for the Pan American General Assembly in Chile.

  Council Member Vasquez mentioned she heard Kaleidoscope recently sold, and was
  wondering if it would be possible to get an update on that in the near future. City Manager
  Wilberg stated staff will provide an update as soon as they can.

 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

 Council Member Bucknum

 Council Member Bucknum stated she and several Council Members attended Mission Viejo Chamber
 of Commerce’s Women in Business Awards Luncheon, and congratulated Valorie Green on the
 Legacy Award. She added that Valorie owned her own restaurant and even started Restaurant Week,
 which is actually this week. She encouraged everyone to view the Chambers website, and partake and
 support the local restaurants in Mission Viejo. Council Member Bucknum gave kudos to the Chamber
 for putting on a great event honoring women leaders in the community. She mentioned that she and
 the Mayor attended the 22nd Annual Mobility 21 Summit, she also attended Bathgate’s Walk to
 School Day Event. She added that she Council Member Ruesch attended the Annual Saddleback
 College Foundation Gala to support students at the Mission Viejo Campus and thanked Saddleback
 College for being such a great partner. She encouraged everyone to attend the Los Osos project walk
 through tomorrow at 4:30pm and provide their input, followed by an evening of unity and light for
City Council Minutes  8  October 10, 2023
  Israel at 6pm on the Village Green, a candlelight vigil the city is partnering with the local Chabad,
 Rabbi Marcus, and several other houses of worship. Council Member Bucknum stated she is happy to
 hear that the City is analyzing short-term rentals, and taking the opportunity to capture transient
 occupant tax TOT. Lastly, she referred to the sale of the Kaleidoscope, of which she’d heard, and
 added that she would appreciate a report. She requested Simon Property clean up the slope along the
 freeway, which is an eyesore as you come into Mission Viejo.

 Council Member Ruesch

 Council Member Ruesch announced that Octoberfest festivities have begun and acknowledged his
 heritage. He stated he had the pleasure of representing the Mayor at the Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast,
 and the honor of speaking on behalf of the City. He added, as a board member of the OCFA he will
 have a report at the next meeting, however, he referred to a video of great importance from OCFA’s
 last meeting that he wished to show this evening. Unfortunately, the video could not be shown. The
 video pertained to the tragedy of PTSD and suicide, and how it affects first responders, fire, sheriffs
 and medical personnel. This video shall be shown at the next Council Meeting on October 24, 2023.

 Council Member Vasquez

 Council Member Vasquez commented that she too attended Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce’s
 Women in Business Awards Luncheon. She also listed the following events she attended; Capo Valley
 Girls Volleyball Team Pink Night, to which the City donated Oso Creek and Recreation Center gift
 certificates. A total of $1,100 was raised, with all donations going to a breast cancer organization in
 Mission Viejo. On September 30, she attended a Girl Scout tree planting event, with three girl scouts
 working towards their Silver Award. She attended Bathgate’s Walk to School Day Event, however,
 she ran, as she was running a little behind. She also attended Lunch at the Landfill with Council
 Member Ruesch, the Character Awards at Bathgate Elementary School, a PTA meeting where she
 was able to relay some of the parents concerns to city staff. And lastly, she shall briefly attend the
 Los Osos Update tomorrow at the North Paseo before heading over to the last Capo Valley Girls
 Volleyball game at Trabuco Hills.

 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated she attended Bathgate’s Walk to School Day Event, spoke on the
 Character Program at Reiley Elementary School, and attended the Character Awards at Bathgate
 Elementary School. She was not able to attend the Annual Saddleback College Foundation Gala this
 year as her grandson had a baseball tournament, and she was busy with baseball, water polo, football,
 volleyball and soccer at the weekend with her grandchildren enjoying the wonderful facilities at
 Mission Viejo. Lastly, she reminded everyone to attend the Walk Against Drugs Event on Saturday,
 October 21 at 8am followed by the Emergency Preparedness Expo. and Community Fair.

 Mayor Goodell

 Mayor Goodell attended Bathgate’s Walk to School Day Event with his crazy socks, Mission Viejo
 Chamber of Commerce’s Women in Business Awards Luncheon, and the 22nd Annual Mobility 21
 Summit. He added, that after hearing one project took 25 years, he came away with the realization of
 how long and complex challenges and issues are in order to accomplish a project. Mayor Goodell
City Council Minutes  9  October 10, 2023
  announced that Cricket is now a part of the 2028 Olympics, with Irvine as the leading contender for
 the venue. He also mentioned that the head representative of the Olympics site findings for
 Netherlands shall be touring Mission Viejo next week. He added that he cannot attend the Walk
 Against Drugs Event next week as he shall be in Santiago. And lastly, he shared an email received by
 Mark Nix, Director or Recreations and Community Services pertaining to a Pickles and Paddles
 Fundraising Tournament benefiting the Orange County Sports Commission and Community. He
 congratulated Coach Yvonne Bustamante at the Felipe Tennis and Recreation Center and club member
 David Lee who brought home the gold and took first place in the advance players bracket at the event.

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 9:30 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting in honor and memory of those who have lost their lives in Israel
 and Gaza in the past few days to Tuesday, October 24, 2023, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________
 Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 Approved at the meeting of October 24, 2023

City Council Minutes  10  October 10, 2023
